techniques.name: Minimal inner agent loop
techniques.gist: LLM + tools + environment feedback in a loop; the harness just executes and echoes. Ball: ~300 lines of Go, three tools. Anthropic: gather context → act → verify → repeat.
techniques.verdict: Delegated by design: the engine drives the Claude Code CLI, which IS the inner loop; our framework is deliberately the outer layer.

techniques.name: Fresh-context outer loop over durable state
techniques.gist: Ralph: `while :; do cat PROMPT.md | claude; done` — fresh session every iteration, all state in files/git. Anthropic ran ~2,000 such sessions to build a C compiler.
techniques.verdict: Our loops resume a pinned session, so context accumulates — the opposite. Landing: a LOOP-WIDE per-arm toggle "fresh session each iteration" in the engine; re-orientation via the T21 progress ledger; dock toggle + convention doc.

techniques.name: Outer work-queue harness decides completion
techniques.gist: A harness above the agent loop holds a queue, runs attempts, and itself decides done/again — "the task stays alive beyond the point where the model would have said: I am done" (Ronacher).
techniques.verdict: The queue kind end-to-end: stash as work queue, consume-on-land, verify phases + reply ladder decide. Baseline: queue resume, "Activation resets phase state", queue binding requirements.

techniques.name: Plan-then-build phase separation
techniques.gist: Two-mode loops: a planning prompt refreshing a prioritized plan, a building prompt executing the top item (Huntley); initializer vs coding agent (Anthropic); plan mode then one-shot (Cherny).
techniques.verdict: Goal loops jump straight to WORKING_STATE. Landing: optional PLANNING_STATE ahead of WORKING_STATE producing/refreshing a plan file; the dock state-machine panel already has the section grammar.

techniques.name: Orchestrator–workers fan-out
techniques.gist: A lead agent spawns 3–5 parallel workers and synthesizes; Anthropic production: +90.2% over single-agent at ~15× tokens.
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: in-turn subagents belong to the CLI; a harness-level LLM orchestrator contradicts one-driven-session-per-tab, and Ronacher’s mixed-write subagent failures caution against it. Human + dock is our orchestrator.

techniques.name: Uncoordinated parallel agents, git task claiming
techniques.gist: No orchestrator: parallel agents claim tasks via lock-file commits, merge each other, self-select "the next most obvious problem" (C-compiler run).
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: concurrent writers on one repo are out of scope — tabs are per-repo, and orphaned-run double-drive history is exactly why the XOR coordinator exists.

techniques.name: Heartbeat tick, idle sentinel, defer-while-busy
techniques.gist: Periodic "anything need attention?" turn; a bare HEARTBEAT_OK reply is suppressed; heartbeats defer while a run is active (Steinberger’s OpenClaw).
techniques.verdict: Independent convergence on our design: engine tick guards + witnessed-reply freshness = defer-while-busy; the sentinel ladder (LOOP_DONE / NEEDS_HUMAN, final-line anchoring) lives in docs/loop-driven-agent-convention.md.

techniques.name: A runnable check closes the loop
techniques.gist: The loudest consensus (7 sources): give the loop a machine-checkable pass/fail and it closes on its own; the verifier must be near-perfect or the agent solves the wrong problem. Cherny: a real feedback loop "will 2-3x the quality".
techniques.verdict: Our VERIFICATION_STATE is agent-self-reported (sentinels). Landing: optional per-arm verify COMMAND on goal/queue loops — sentinel only counts if the check passes; failing output goes back into WORKING_STATE; dock param box + eval scenario where a lying sentinel is caught.

techniques.name: Escalating stop-gates
techniques.gist: Grades of stop-gating: in-prompt iterate → /goal condition re-checked per turn → Stop hook blocking turn-end → fresh-context verifier.
techniques.verdict: Our ladder mirrors it: composed verify prompts per phase, sentinel-gated exits, deny fences, caps, NEEDS_HUMAN. Baseline: the state-machine parameter panel requirement (badges, transitions, terminal outcomes).

techniques.name: Adversarial fresh-context / second-model review
techniques.gist: A reviewer that didn’t produce the change grades it: fresh subagent seeing only diff + criteria (Anthropic); a different model entirely (Steinberger’s GPT-5/Gemini/Oracle steps).
techniques.verdict: Our verify phase is graded by the session that did the work. Landing: optional second-opinion step reusing the CliPromptClassifier one-shot machinery — fresh CLI call sees diff + goal, returns confirm/refute; refute → escalate with reason; audit records the verdict.

techniques.name: Evidence, not assertions
techniques.gist: The agent shows the test output / command result / screenshot instead of claiming success — "works for sessions you weren’t watching".
techniques.verdict: Verify prompts don’t demand shown evidence and the audit records sends, not proof. Landing: verification templates require pasted check output ahead of the sentinel; briefing rule; sent-history keeps the evidence blob.

techniques.name: Externalized done-ness ledger
techniques.gist: Done-ness lives in a machine-checkable artifact: JSON feature list with passes:false booleans flipped only after verification; fixes "premature victory declaration".
techniques.verdict: The queue stash IS an on-disk work ledger the loop drains, with cumulative sent-history as the done record (queue-loop-visibility).

techniques.name: Browser-level E2E self-verification
techniques.gist: Verify as a user would: Cherny’s Chrome-extension loop, Anthropic’s Puppeteer gate on passes:true, Steinberger’s single chrome-devtools MCP "to close the loop".
techniques.verdict: Repo conventions mandate it already: docs/claude-web/browser-testing.md, docs/detached-verification-convention.md, System Tests + E2E eval console surfaces.

techniques.name: Hard iteration caps + explicit stopping conditions
techniques.gist: Terminate on completion OR a hard cap; real loops also end at plan exhaustion or the model’s capability ceiling (honestly reported in the compiler run).
techniques.verdict: Turn caps with terminal capped status are baseline; the loop-eval cap scenario tests them; LOOP-WIDE section exposes them.

techniques.name: Human checkpoints, unchanged review bar
techniques.gist: Autonomy bracketed by humans: clear task in, blocker pauses during, human review out — "the same exact bar regardless of whether the code was written by the model" (Cherny, at 80–90% model-written).
techniques.verdict: Suggest mode on every kind, NEEDS_HUMAN, operator gate, escalate statuses. Baseline: suggest-mode pending requirement + gate disclosure rules.

techniques.name: Deterministic fences around the loop
techniques.gist: Non-LLM enforcement: git hooks running jscpd/knip/ast-grep (Steinberger), CI regression gates (compiler run), product hooks ("deterministic, unlike advisory CLAUDE.md").
techniques.verdict: Word-boundary deny-lists (routine + reply), per-arm trims, operator gate, kill switch. Baseline: the three deny-list requirements.

techniques.name: LLM-as-judge: rubric-scored, weakest gate
techniques.gist: A single rubric-scored judge call was Anthropic’s most consistent grader — and the SDK post still ranks model-judging LAST, behind rules-based and visual checks ("generally not very robust").
techniques.verdict: The CLI-backed classifier judges routine matches behind the stub’s contract with fallback, and every verdict still passes threshold/deny/cap/gate fences — exactly the weakest-gate posture. Baseline: CLI classifier requirement.

techniques.name: Reference-oracle fallback
techniques.gist: Mix a known-good reference (GCC) with the agent’s output so the loop can bisect blame and shrink the frontier gradually.
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: needs a domain with a reference implementation; general product repos have none.

techniques.name: Context as a finite attention budget
techniques.gist: "Context rot": curate the smallest high-signal token set. Huntley budgets ~30% for specs/plans; reports 200k advertised ≈ 147–152k practical.
techniques.verdict: Not applicable at harness level: the window is the CLI’s to manage; our lever is keeping injections small — the briefing frame is compact by design.

techniques.name: Compaction (summarize and reinitiate)
techniques.gist: Near the limit, distill the conversation and restart with the summary (shipped in Claude Code / the SDK).
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: CLI-internal shipped mechanism.

techniques.name: Progress files as cross-iteration memory
techniques.gist: Amnesiac iterations re-orient from disk: claude-progress.txt + git history, frequently-updated READMEs, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md; read on entry, commit + update on exit.
techniques.verdict: Nothing asks our driven agents to keep durable progress state. Landing: progress-ledger contract in docs/loop-driven-agent-convention.md + a default briefing rule; engine optionally composes the ledger tail into the next prompt. Prerequisite for rank 2.

techniques.name: Fresh-session reset over in-context correction
techniques.gist: Failed attempts poison the window: throw away and re-prompt (Cherny), two-strikes /clear rule (guide), delete-and-regenerate the stale plan (Huntley).
techniques.verdict: On verify failure we re-propose into the same session, then escalate. Landing: after N failed verify cycles, a per-arm "reset iteration" — fresh session with step + distilled failure summary — before escalating. Pairs with rank 2 plumbing.

techniques.name: Subagent fan-out for context isolation
techniques.gist: Reads fan out to isolated subagents returning condensed summaries (Huntley: up to 500 for reads, exactly 1 for builds); Ronacher: write-capable subagents misbehaved.
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: CLI-internal (Task tool); the driven agent already has it.

techniques.name: Persistent instruction file as institutional memory
techniques.gist: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md reloaded every session: Cherny folds every observed mistake in; the guide says keep it lean; Steinberger runs ~800 lines — sources disagree on size, not mechanism.
techniques.verdict: Repo CLAUDE.md + the operator-editable briefing rules injected into every loop send (loop-agent-briefing, shipped).

techniques.name: Quiet tools that log details to files
techniques.gist: Verifiers print a few lines and log the rest to a file the agent can read on demand; measured token savings from concise tool responses.
techniques.verdict: The detached-verification convention’s log-file + terminal-marker contract is this exact rule for long checks.

techniques.name: Mid-loop reinforcement injection
techniques.gist: The harness re-states objectives after tool calls, hints after failures, uses "echo tools" reflecting the agent’s own task list back (Ronacher’s production harness).
techniques.verdict: The briefing frame composed at the send choke point re-states rules on every loop send; the FLAG: channel carries signals back.

techniques.name: Just-in-time retrieval over pre-loading
techniques.gist: Keep lightweight identifiers, load data at runtime via agentic search; pre-load only cheap always-needed files.
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: CLI-internal shipped behavior.

techniques.name: Sandboxed full-permission (YOLO) execution
techniques.gist: Remove approval friction INSIDE containment: $5-capped Fly.io org (Willison), claude-yolo in Docker (Ronacher), skip-permissions + hourly backups (Steinberger).
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: permission mode / OS sandboxing are host decisions outside the Product; the harness’s containment is gate + deny + caps, which exist.

techniques.name: Risk-scoped permissioning
techniques.gist: Between approve-everything and skip-everything: allowlists, auto-accept only for safely-verifiable loops (test iteration), classifier-gated auto mode.
techniques.verdict: Threshold-gated drive sends, per-arm deny trims, suggest-vs-drive dial, operator gate. Baseline: threshold gating + per-arm deny requirements.

techniques.name: Start small, then scale the automation
techniques.gist: Run the loop on one item, verify behavior, refine on the first 2–3 failures, then scale.
techniques.verdict: Suggest mode is the ramp (watch what it WOULD send), and the queue arm preview shows binding + items before any send.

techniques.name: Parallelism stratified by review cost / blast radius
techniques.gist: The human review bottleneck governs loop count: Willison parallelizes only low-review-cost tracks; Steinberger sizes by blast radius; Cherny runs 5 local + 5–10 cloud.
techniques.verdict: Multi-tab dock under one operator, XOR coordinator (one armed loop per agent), loop badges + binding disclosure keep each track legible; the stratification judgment stays human, as the sources practice.

techniques.name: Fleet bookkeeping + phone-reachable monitoring
techniques.gist: Self-reported terminal titles, browser/phone terminals for checking long runs (VibeTunnel), phone-started morning sessions (Cherny).
techniques.verdict: Claude Web’s founding premise: phone dock, waiting badges, live loop decision readout, phase strip. Baseline: dock disclosure + live-state requirements.

techniques.name: Message queueing + stall auto-continue
techniques.gist: Queue "continue" messages so long runs keep going; detect stalls and auto-continue (CodeLooper).
techniques.verdict: The queue kind IS productized message queueing; the drive no-reply escape is engine-level stall detection.

techniques.name: Durable execution: checkpoint, resume, retry
techniques.gist: Resume from where errors occurred instead of restarting; checkpoints make risk cheap; rainbow deployments keep in-flight agents alive.
techniques.verdict: Detached backend-owned runs with reattach, loop resume preserving sent-history, operator-stop-is-not-error. Baseline: resume + stopped-not-errored requirements.

techniques.name: Explicit effort-scaling rules
techniques.gist: Prompt-embedded sizing: simple fact-find = 1 agent / 3–10 calls; complex research = 10+ subagents.
techniques.verdict: Not applicable: sizing governs coordinator fan-out; our loops drive exactly one session — no fan-out decision exists.

techniques.name: Self-improving prompts from failure transcripts
techniques.gist: Feed the loop’s failure transcripts back to the model: prompt diagnosis, tool-description rewriting (40% task-time reduction).
techniques.verdict: We collect the raw material (audit trail, debug snapshot) but never feed it back. Landing: console "improve this loop" action → one-shot CLI over snapshot + audit rows → suggested prompt/briefing edits, operator-accepted, never auto-applied.

techniques.name: Negative results: automation that didn’t stick
techniques.gist: Ronacher dropped slash commands, hooks, print mode, write-capable subagents; Steinberger dropped worktrees, calls MCPs "context poison"; one compiler agent pkill-ed its own loop.
techniques.verdict: Not a feature — calibration evidence. It supports current choices: single driven session, conversational prompts over slash automation, MCP skepticism.
